title: Japan's household confidence recovered modestly in August while durable-purchase timing improved beneath persistent price expectations
source_unit: Japan Cabinet Office Economic and Social Research Institute, monthly Consumer Confidence Survey, August 2026

observations.period: August 2026; household confidence and purchase timing

denominator.unit: valid responding households in the August 2026 survey; 4,347 two-or-more-person and 2,327 one-person households

observations.method: Japan Cabinet Office monthly Consumer Confidence Survey using a three-stage sample of households and mail-plus-online collection; the August survey covered 8,400 selected households, with 6,674 valid responses and a 79.5 percent response rate. The confidence index is the simple average of livelihood, income-growth, employment, and durable-goods purchase-timing indicators for two-or-more-person households.
observations.uncertainty: The confidence and purchase-timing indexes measure reported perceptions, not realized purchases, income, employment, or household welfare; the published summary's headline index is for two-or-more-person households even though the valid-response frame includes one-person households.
observations.subgroup: Japanese households, with separate two-or-more-person and one-person sampling frames; headline component indexes reported for two-or-more-person households.
observations.counterinterpretation: A modest confidence recovery and stronger durable-purchase timing can reflect seasonal timing, price changes, credit access, or compositional movement rather than broad improvement in material security or realized consumption.

observations.period: August 2026; component divergence beneath the confidence recovery

denominator.unit: valid responding two-or-more-person households used for the published component indexes

livelihood_index.unit: seasonally adjusted index; up 1.0 point from July

income_growth_index.unit: seasonally adjusted index; down 0.5 points from July

employment_index.unit: seasonally adjusted index; down 0.2 points from July

component_divergence.value: Perceived livelihood and durable-purchase timing improved while income-growth and employment perceptions softened

observations.method: Published Cabinet Office component indexes from the same monthly survey and seasonal-adjustment series.
observations.uncertainty: The components are cross-sectional monthly perception measures and do not identify whether the same households changed across items or whether actual income, jobs, and purchases changed.
observations.subgroup: Two-or-more-person households represented in the headline seasonally adjusted consumer-perception series.
observations.counterinterpretation: The component pattern may reflect survey timing, seasonal adjustment, expectations about future conditions, or different respondents rather than a household-level trade-off between livelihood and employment security.

denominator.unit: valid responding two-or-more-person households used for the published price-expectations distribution; item-specific response counts may differ

expect_prices_to_rise.unit: percent expecting prices to rise one year ahead

expect_prices_unchanged.unit: percent expecting prices to remain about unchanged one year ahead

expect_prices_to_fall.unit: percent expecting prices to fall one year ahead

five_percent_plus_expectation.unit: percent expecting prices to rise 5 percent or more one year ahead

observations.method: Cabinet Office price-expectations question about frequently purchased items, collected in the August 15, 2026 survey and reported as an original-series distribution.
observations.uncertainty: Price expectations are subjective and are not a forecast of the official price index or a measure of realized household inflation exposure; the published report notes that item-level response counts can differ.
observations.subgroup: Two-or-more-person households in the published price-expectations series.
observations.counterinterpretation: High expected inflation can coexist with durable-purchase timing improvements if households advance purchases, substitute categories, draw on savings, or face different price exposure.

related_sources.claim: Japanese-language official release index and links to August 2026 summary, full report, and e-Stat tables.
Japan's government statistics portal provides household-type and long-run tables for the Consumer Confidence Survey.
English Cabinet Office summary provides the August 2026 sample, response rate, confidence index, components, and price-expectations headline figures.

boundary: This record adds a Japan-specific household-perception and purchase-timing surface to the comparative consumer atlas. It does not establish realized purchases, household income or employment change, price-index inflation, financial stress, cultural preference, or causal effects.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Cabinet Office English summary and August 2026 Japanese summary/full report were reviewed for sample design, response counts, confidence and component indexes, price-expectations distribution, field date, collection mode, and rotating-panel structure.
